messages:
alex_lewis: Quick check — I'm about to open a TF change that: creates a small dedicated GPU nodepool with capacity reservations, tags CRs for billing, and wires node bootstrap secrets to Secrets Manager. Wanted to call out a couple constraints before I send the PR.

maria_g: SGTM. Which instance families are you planning to reserve? h100-only or mixed? Also curious about the CR type: ephemeral vs targeted reservation.

alex_lewis: Thinking h100 for the reserved pool (predictable latency for infra tests) and a mixed spot pool (p4d/p4de) for bursty jobs. Using targeted capacity_reservation so we get a zone-affined reservation and can keep az locality.

sam_reed: Quick note — if we use targeted CRs we need to ensure the ASG/nodegroup uses the right placement group/az in the TF so pods with azAffinity land. Watch the k8s label flow.

toni_ops: Also +1 on tags. Please add tags: {"CostCenter":"infra-staging","Owner":"ml-infra","env":"staging"} on both the CR and instances so billing maps. We need the tags on the EC2 resources (not just the nodegroup).

alex_lewis: Will do. Draft of the TF snippet I plan to include (aws):

```hcl
resource "aws_capacity_reservation" "gpu_h100_reservation" {
  instance_type         = "hpc.g5.48xlarge" # example, adjust if needed
  availability_zone     = var.az
  instance_count        = 2
  tenancy               = "default"
  tags = {
    CostCenter = "infra-staging"
    Owner      = "ml-infra"
    env        = "staging"
    purpose    = "dedicated-gpu-pool"
  }
}

resource "aws_launch_template" "gpu_node_lt" {
  name_prefix   = "gpu-node-"
  image_id      = data.aws_ami.gpu.id
  instance_type = "hpc.g5.48xlarge"
  tag_specifications {
    resource_type = "instance"
    tags = {
      CostCenter = "infra-staging"
      Owner      = "ml-infra"
      env        = "staging"
    }
  }
}

resource "aws_autoscaling_group" "gpu_reserved_asg" {
  name                      = "gpu-reserved-asg"
  desired_capacity          = 2
  max_size                  = 2
  min_size                  = 2
  launch_template {
    id      = aws_launch_template.gpu_node_lt.id
    version = "$Latest"
  }
  capacity_reservation_specification {
    capacity_reservation_preference = "open"
    capacity_reservation_target {
      capacity_reservation_id = aws_capacity_reservation.gpu_h100_reservation.id
    }
  }
}
```

maria_g: That looks good. Small suggestion: use `capacity_reservation_preference = "none"` vs `open` depending on how strict we want the match. If we set to `open` it might still place on other instances if CR cannot fulfill. Test in a canary AZ.

sam_reed: For kube-level wiring: add node labels/taints in launch template user-data or bootstrap script. e.g. add `--node-labels=instance-type=gpu-h100` and taint `gpu=true:NoSchedule` so only GPU workloads land. Also ensure bootstrap secret (kubelet token/certs) are pulled from Secrets Manager.

alex_lewis: Right — planned userdata will place `/etc/kubelet/kubelet.env` with labels and taints. For secret rotation: we currently store the node bootstrap token in aws_secretsmanager_secret + secret_version. I want to add a small lambda rotation to rotate every 90 days. Any ops concerns?

toni_ops: Ops notes: rotating the bootstrap secret requires a rollout plan — nodes created during rotation must be able to bootstrap with both old+new secrets, or we need a transitional window. Prefer: create new secret version, update ASG launch template to reference it, then drain & replace nodes. ETA: ~10min per node.

maria_g: Also double-check IAM role permissions for the nodes to read Secrets Manager. We had a previous outage because the node role couldn't call `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` in a cross-account scenario. Add that to the TF IAM module.

alex_lewis: Will add an inline policy. Example snippet I'll add to PR:

```hcl
data "aws_iam_policy_document" "node_read_secrets" {
  statement {
    effect = "Allow"
    actions = ["secretsmanager:GetSecretValue"]
    resources = [aws_secretsmanager_secret.node_bootstrap.arn]
  }
}

resource "aws_iam_role_policy" "node_secrets_policy" {
  name   = "node-secrets-policy"
  role   = aws_iam_role.node_role.name
  policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.node_read_secrets.json
}
```

deploy-bot: CI check failed on the existing infra-tests: `TestASGCapacityReservation` — "reservation not found in az us-west-2b"

sam_reed: That CI failure is expected until the TF change creates the CR. For the PR, include a small acceptance test that asserts the `capacity_reservation_id` is set on the ASG in the zone the test runs in. We can mock with localstack for dev runs.

toni_ops: Action items:
- alex_lewis: open PR with TF change + userdata + IAM policy + secrets manager rotation plan (PR should include an explicit node replacement plan).
- alex_lewis: add acceptance test to infra-tests referencing CR id.
- maria_g: review instance sizing and cost estimate (esp h100 SKU).
- sam_reed: add k8s taint/label tests and validate pod scheduling.

alex_lewis: Filing PR now — link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4123 (draft). Will drop in reviewers: @maria_g @sam_reed @toni_ops.

maria_g: thanks — I'll look this afternoon. If we want to be conservative we can start with 1 reserved node and scale to 2 after a canary pass.

alex_lewis: Good call. I'll default to 1 and set a `count` var default 1.

sam_reed: FYI: for the spot/mixed pool, ensure the cluster autoscaler has `--expander=least-waste` and node-selector fallback to avoid scheduling non-gpu pods there.

toni_ops: Noted. I'll coordinate a short maintenance window for node replacement when you rotate the secret.

alex_lewis: Perfect. Thanks all — I'll update the PR after the first CI run and post back here with any surprises. :thumbsup:
